H1.note: the mechanism ends at 'schizophrenia-relevant circuit dysfunction' (H1.5, vague, ungroundable); the second claim targets the last expressible node, synapse pruning, which the title names ('C4A-biased classical complement tagging drives excessive microglial synapse pruning'). The disease link is H1.1's association, signed by PMID:26814963. C4B ('independent effect uncertain'), C1QA and CX3CR1 ('promote or tune') get no claim: no direction stated

H2.note: the chain starts at 'CSMD1 variation' (H2.1, an unsigned association); the mechanism says reduced CSMD1 function removes a brake on complement and so raises risk, i.e. CSMD1 lowers risk

H3.note: the chain ends at 'schizophrenia-relevant endophenotypes' (H3.4, vague), never at schizophrenia, and the mechanism itself says disease genetics do not support NXPH3; the disease claim is read from 'Reduced NXPH3 function ... producing schizophrenia-relevant ... abnormalities'. The phenotype claims target the three abnormalities of H3.3, which the mechanism names as the schizophrenia-relevant ones ('sensory-gating, learning and locomotor abnormalities')

findings.detail: H1.1 ends at schizophrenia and H1.2 restarts at 'C1QA and C4A/C4B'; the association is a premise placed first, not a link (H2.1 to H2.2 has the same shape).

H1.3 ends at 'microglial synapse pruning' and H1.4 starts at CX3CR1, a side input; H1.4 to H1.5 links only after merging 'normal ... maturation and pruning' with 'excessive microglial synapse pruning'.
H2.2 (CSMD1 inhibits the classical pathway) and H2.3 ('reduced CSMD1 function' increases synaptic opsonization) both start at CSMD1; they are parallel restatements, not a chain.

no H3 step's object is the next step's subject: alpha-neurexins / 'NXPH3-alpha-neurexin signaling', 'normal synaptic circuit function' / 'loss of NXPH3 function', 'abnormal learning, locomotion and sensorimotor gating' / 'abnormal synaptic circuit function'.

H1's mechanism ends at 'schizophrenia-relevant circuit dysfunction', not at schizophrenia; its disease claim composes directly only through H1.1's association and mechanistically only through H2.5, a step of another hypothesis, so it gets a second claim at synapse pruning, the node its title names.

H3 ends at 'schizophrenia-relevant endophenotypes' and never reaches schizophrenia, so its implied claim (NXPH3 lowers risk) has no route; its phenotype claims (the three H3.3 abnormalities) each compose in one step.

rs1150754 is cited as the C4A/C4B locus but the authors report it for TNXB (GWAS Catalog maps it to C4A, C4B by position, 47 kb from C4B and 80 kb from C4A); it is a different signal from the C4 structural alleles of PMID:26814963.
PMID:22632727 is cited for classical-pathway and C1q/C4-opsonization steps but shows CR3/C3-dependent microglial engulfment in the mouse retinogeniculate system, with no C1q, C4 or classical pathway.
STRING GO-enrichment records (GO:0006958, GO:0098883, GO:1903028) are cited as evidence for signed steps; they report that the input genes share a GO term, nothing about one thing acting on another.
UniProt Q96PZ7 is cited for CSMD1 inhibiting complement but its function text is only 'Potential suppressor of squamous cell carcinomas'.
PMID:40112933 shows CSMD1 domains inhibit the classical C3 convertase in assays; it never shows that losing CSMD1 increases C1q/C4 deposition on synapses, which is the step.

MP:0001488 'increased startle reflex' is cited for abnormal sensorimotor gating, but startle amplitude is not prepulse inhibition; no cited record measures gating, so the gating claim has only the refuting null.

every citation the run gave these steps (H1.4: its maturation half; H3.3: its gating part) was excluded: none states complement to pruning, CX3CR1 to maturation, pruning to circuit dysfunction or to schizophrenia, CSMD1 loss to synaptic opsonization, NXPH3 to circuit function, or NXPH3 loss to gating; H1.3's only support is a background sentence of a citation the run lists as contradicting.
both CSMD1 GWAS records give the risk allele as '?', so the run cannot say which way CSMD1 variation acts, yet its mechanism assumes it reduces CSMD1 function.

H1 is rated 'high' with support 'grounded', but no chain citation states complement to pruning or pruning to dysfunction; only the C4A association (H1.1) and pathway membership (H1.2) hold, and its own contradicting citation reports lower C1q in schizophrenia.

AGR:MGI:2137383:DOID:5419 (Csmd1 knockout curated as a schizophrenia model, no publication) is the only record tying CSMD1 loss to schizophrenia, but no step cites it; it is a mouse disease-model annotation, not the association H2.1 states, so it attaches nowhere.

H1's supporting records HPA:ENSG00000173372 (C1QA in microglia), STRING:C1QA-C4A and STRING:C1QA-C4B (database 0.90, experiments 0) and AGR:MGI:88223:MP:0002910 (C1qa knockout, abnormal excitatory postsynaptic currents) state no step: the run has no expression, binding or C1QA-to-synaptic-current step.
H2's supporting records HPA:ENSG00000183117 (CSMD1 in brain neurons) and AGR:MGI:2137383:MP:0001489 (Csmd1 knockout, decreased startle reflex) state no step.

PMID:26814963 says 'In mice, C4 mediated synapse elimination', and PMID:38301948 that C4A has been 'implicated ... in excessive elimination of synapses in schizophrenia': direct C4 to pruning statements the chain never uses; H1 routes through the classical pathway, whose own citations do not state pruning.

PMID:38301948, listed as contradicting H1, is the only cited text that states H1.3 (its background: C4A contributes to synapse removal through the C1q-initiated classical axis); the run cites it against itself and its chain citations for the step say less. That one review sentence carries H1's title claim (C4A to synapse pruning, belief 12/25).

PMID:38301948 reports lower C1QA mRNA in schizophrenia prefrontal cortex and lower CSF C1qA in first-episode psychosis, against H1's excess-complement premise for C1QA; the mechanism lists it but does not reconcile it, and no step links C1QA to schizophrenia for it to refute.

PMID:PPR1218914, listed as contradicting H2, states H2.1 in its background (CSMD1 a GWAS risk gene); its result, unchanged CSMD1 expression in schizophrenia brain, bears only on the mechanism's 'reduced functional output' premise, which no step states.

AGR:MGI:1336188:MP:0002169 ('no abnormal phenotype detected') is for Nxph3<tm1Mami>, while the positive learning, locomotion and startle annotations are for Nxph3<tm1.1Mami>, all from PMID:16055736; the run lists the null as contradicting but does not say which allele to believe. Attached as refutes to each H3.3 statement.

the run's 'abnormal learning' generalises the only cited record, MGI 'abnormal spatial learning'; grounded at MP:0001463 because MP has no plain 'abnormal learning' and MP:0002063 adds memory and conditioning.

H3 treats increased startle in Nxph3-knockout mice as schizophrenia-relevant, while H2's supporting record AGR:MGI:2137383:MP:0001489 shows decreased startle in Csmd1-knockout mice; the run does not reconcile the two directions.
the same GO process (synapse pruning, GO:0098883, synonym 'synapse elimination') is a 'process' in H1 and a 'phenotype' in H2.
CCDC136 is listed as unexplained and appears in no hypothesis.

no ontology term for the alpha-neurexin family (PR has neurexin-1-alpha and neurexin-3-alpha only, no family term); made BLN:AlphaNeurexins so H3.1's binding step is a statement rather than set_valued.

UniProt says C4A/C4B are components of the classical pathway and CX3CR1 'participates in' synaptic pruning; I read membership and participation as a positive effect, but BioLean has no participates-in to effect rule to make that explicit.

evidence bearing on a hypothesis claim that no statement carries (GWAS:NXPH3:no-association and OT:NXPH3 at 0.00 against NXPH3 to schizophrenia; PMID:38301948's lower C1q against an unclaimed C1QA role) has nowhere to go as refutes; it is excluded under the nearest step with category 'other'.

a blanket MGI 'no abnormal phenotype detected' for one allele refutes each specific abnormal phenotype with the same kind and weight as the positive annotation for another allele, so H3_3a and H3_3b come out contested (4/9 against 4/9) and H3_3c refuted (disbelief 4/5) on that null alone, although it may never have tested learning, locomotion or gating.

the unsigned H2_1 is 'established' (belief 9/10) from two GWAS rows, an Open Targets score built partly from those GWAS, and two background sentences restating the same association; the evidence is not independent, and an established verdict on an association with no direction may read as more than it is.

H2_1 keeps five citations and H1_1b one, but unsigned associations cannot compose, so CSMD1's best-supported link to schizophrenia adds nothing to H2's arms, which run through unsupported H2.3 to H2.5 or borrowed H1.3.
an Open Targets association score (an aggregate of GWAS, literature mining and animal models) has no evidence kind; kept as curatedDb for the unsigned H2.1.
UniProt 'By similarity' text is crossSpecies but names no source species, so it gets no taxon and the lint cannot see the species gap.

render.py composes over all statements, so H1's mechanistic arm uses H2.5 and H2's pathway arm uses H1.3; a hypothesis gets routes its own chain never made (intended in v2, where the report counts borrowed steps).

audit.reason: no_direction is defined only for record types that cannot carry a sign (STRING edge, OT score, expression level); P49238 is a UniProt curatedDb function text, which can carry a sign and simply states no direction ('regulating synapse maturation'), so 'other' is the only fitting category. Keeping P49238 for pruning (H1_4a) and excluding it for maturation was correct.
guide v2 adds 'undirected' (names both ends, no direction, for a signed step), which is exactly this case.
